meta.name: Review and remediate Kubernetes manifests in GitHub PRs with GPT-4.1

parameters.content:
## AI Kubernetes Security & Policy Agent — Manifest Analysis, Auto-Remediation & PR Review

This is a manifest-review agent, not a fixed linter pipeline. A GitHub pull request touching Kubernetes YAML manifests triggers the flow. An LLM AGENT decides for itself which checks to run against the changed manifests — it can call a privileged-container scanner, an RBAC/permissions analyzer, an exposed-services detector, a resource-limits checker, and a policy/RAG tool over your org's Pod Security Standards / OPA-Gatekeeper policies — before writing a structured findings report. Wherever it finds an issue, the agent also generates a corrected, secure version of the manifest. Findings + secure manifests are logged for audit, posted back to the PR as a review comment, and a human must approve before the agent's suggested fix is committed to a remediation branch and opened as its own PR (or pushed as a suggested-change commit) — nothing is auto-merged.

### How it works
1. GitHub Trigger - PR Opened/Updated fires on pull_request events (opened, synchronize) for repos containing Kubernetes manifests
2. Set - Config extracts PR number, repo, branch, changed file paths, and a sessionId (PR number) for continuity across pushes
3. Get - PR Manifest Files pulls the actual changed YAML content from GitHub before handing it to the agent
4. AI Agent - K8s Security Reviewer (GPT-4.1 + session memory) is given five tools — Tool - Scan Privileged Containers, Tool - Scan RBAC Permissions, Tool - Scan Exposed Services, Tool - Scan Resource Limits, Tool - RAG Search Security Policies — and decides on its own which to call, possibly more than once across multiple manifests, before writing findings AND a generated secure manifest for each flagged file
5. Set - Parse Agent Output extracts the agent's structured JSON (findings per manifest/category, overallRisk, verdict, securedManifests)
6. Postgres - Log Security Review persists every review into a k8s_manifest_reviews table for audit history and trend tracking
7. GitHub - Post Review Comment always posts the full findings (plus a diff-style preview of proposed fixes) back to the PR, regardless of verdict
8. IF - Issues Found only continues toward remediation when the agent actually flagged something; clean manifests just get the passing comment and stop
9. Slack - Request Remediation Approval posts the proposed secure manifests to the platform/security team; Wait - For Remediation Approval pauses on the approval webhook
10. IF - Remediation Approved gates the actual write: approved fixes get committed to a new branch and opened as a remediation PR linked back to the original; rejected ones just notify Slack so a human edits manually

### How to set up
1. Import this workflow into n8n
2. Add GitHub credentials (repo scope, PR + branch write access) on the trigger and all GitHub nodes
3. Add an OpenAI (or compatible) credential on the OpenAI Chat Model, plus a Vector Store credential on the RAG tool pointed at your Pod Security Standards / OPA-Gatekeeper / internal K8s policy docs
4. Wire the four scanner tools to wherever these actually run (a CI job via HTTP callback, kube-score/kubesec/Polaris-style scanners, or an Execute Command node if n8n has the binaries installed locally) — these are read-only static analyses, never applied to a live cluster
5. Add a Postgres credential and create the `k8s_manifest_reviews` table (columns per the node's sticky note)
6. Add Slack credentials on the remediation-approval and notification nodes
7. Point Wait - For Remediation Approval's resume webhook at your reviewer UI's approve/reject action
8. Open a test PR touching a Kubernetes manifest (e.g. a Deployment with `privileged: true` and no resource limits) to run end-to-end

## 1. PR Trigger, Manifest Retrieval & Tool-Calling Security Agent

- **GitHub Trigger - PR Opened/Updated** — fires on pull_request opened/synchronize events for repos containing K8s manifests.
- **Set - Config** — extracts PR number, repo, branch, changed file paths, and derives a sessionId (PR number) for continuity across pushes.
- **Get - PR Manifest Files** — fetches the changed YAML manifest content from GitHub for the agent to analyze.
- **Tool - Scan Privileged Containers** — callable tool; the agent decides when to check for `privileged: true`, `allowPrivilegeEscalation`, host namespaces (hostPID/hostNetwork/hostIPC), and root-user containers.
- **Tool - Scan RBAC Permissions** — callable tool; the agent decides when to check Roles/ClusterRoles/RoleBindings for wildcard verbs/resources, cluster-admin bindings, or overly broad ServiceAccount permissions.
- **Tool - Scan Exposed Services** — callable tool; the agent decides when to check Services/Ingresses for unintended NodePort/LoadBalancer exposure, missing NetworkPolicies, or public ingress without auth.
- **Tool - Scan Resource Limits** — callable tool; the agent decides when to check containers for missing/absent CPU-memory requests and limits, or limits set unreasonably high relative to node capacity.
- **Tool - RAG Search Security Policies** — callable tool backed by a vector store of the org's Pod Security Standards, OPA-Gatekeeper constraints, and past review precedents.
- **OpenAI Chat Model** — the LLM powering the agent. 🔑
- **Window Buffer Memory** — session-keyed memory (by PR number) so re-review after a push considers prior findings.
- **AI Agent - K8s Security Reviewer** — orchestrates: calls whichever tools are relevant per manifest, then returns structured findings, an overall risk rating, a verdict, and a generated secure manifest for each flagged file.

## 2. Audit Logging, PR Comment & Remediation Gate

- **Set - Parse Agent Output** — extracts the agent's structured JSON (findings[], overallRisk, verdict, securedManifests[]).
- **Postgres - Log Security Review** — inserts every review into `k8s_manifest_reviews` (prNumber, repo, findings, overallRisk, verdict, securedManifests, createdAt) — audit trail and trend data.
- **GitHub - Post Review Comment** — always posts findings + a preview of proposed secure manifests back to the PR, whatever the verdict.
- **IF - Issues Found** — only continues toward remediation when findings is non-empty; clean manifests stop here.

nodes.name: Sticky Note - Human Approval & Remediation PR

parameters.content:
## 3. Human Approval & Remediation PR (only when issues are found)

- **Slack - Request Remediation Approval** — posts the flagged findings + generated secure manifests to the platform/security team with Approve/Reject options.
- **IF - Remediation Approved** — the single gate before any secure manifest is written to a branch.
- **GitHub - Create Remediation Branch** — branches off the PR head to hold the fix.
- **GitHub - Commit Secure Manifests** — commits each generated secure manifest to the remediation branch.
- **GitHub - Open Remediation PR** — opens a PR from the remediation branch back into the original PR's branch, linked in the description.
- **Slack - Post Remediation PR Link** — notifies the team the fix PR is ready to review/merge.
- **Slack - Post Rejection Notice** — notifies the team when the proposed fix was rejected, so a human edits the manifests manually instead.

parameters.name: search_security_policies
parameters.description: Semantic search over the org's Pod Security Standards, OPA-Gatekeeper constraint templates, and past manifest review precedents. Use this to check the change against internal policy, not just generic best practice.

parameters.text:
=You are a senior Kubernetes security engineer reviewing manifests changed in a pull request.

Repo: {{ $json.repoOwner }}/{{ $json.repoName }} | Branch: {{ $json.branch }}
PR #{{ $json.prNumber }} by {{ $json.prAuthor }}: "{{ $json.prTitle }}"

Changed files:
{{ $json.files.map(f => '- ' + f.filename).join('\n') }}

You have five tools: scan_privileged_containers, scan_rbac_permissions, scan_exposed_services, scan_resource_limits, search_security_policies. For each changed manifest, call whichever scanners are relevant to its kind (Deployment/Pod → privileged + resource limits; Role/RoleBinding/ServiceAccount → RBAC; Service/Ingress → exposure) — call tools more than once across multiple files as needed. Do not guess scanner findings; only state what the tools returned. Use search_security_policies to check any ambiguous case against org policy before flagging it.

If earlier turns exist in this conversation (same PR), treat this as a re-review after a new push and note what changed since the prior review.

For every finding, assign a severity ('low'|'medium'|'high'|'critical') and a category ('privileged'|'rbac'|'exposure'|'resource_limits'|'other'). For every file with at least one 'medium'+ finding, generate a corrected, secure version of that manifest's full YAML that fixes the issues found (add resource limits, drop privileges, add runAsNonRoot, restrict RBAC verbs/resources, add NetworkPolicy, etc.) while preserving the manifest's original intent and unrelated fields. Set overallRisk to the highest severity present, and verdict to 'issues_found' if findings is non-empty, else 'pass'.

Return ONLY a JSON object (no markdown fences, no commentary) with keys: summary (2-4 sentences), findings (array of {file, category, description, severity}), overallRisk ('low'|'medium'|'high'|'critical'|'none'), verdict ('pass'|'issues_found'), securedManifests (array of {file, yaml, changesSummary}).

parameters.columns: pr_number, repo, author, findings, overall_risk, verdict, secured_manifests, created_at
